Hi Soojin,

I signed up for Redwood yesterday (trial) after seeing the GitHub integration mention on your docs. We're evaluating a few approaches for embedding repository data and code search in our product and I'd like to get a short demo focused on architecture and permissions. A few quick questions before we lock a slot:

- Do you support installation as a GitHub App across multiple orgs with a single token per customer?
- Are webhook deliveries retried by Redwood if our endpoint is flaky? We saw a 403 when trying the self-serve install (screenshot attached).
- For customers who want to keep code on-prem, do you have a private deployment option or does it require a dedicated gateway?

Would love a 30–40 minute time where I can bring our engineering lead (PST). Our ideal window this week is 2pm–5pm PST.

Attaching the screenshot of the webhook error: webhook-error-screenshot.png

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alex / Soojin — thanks for the details and for booking the slot. Confirming Wed 2/17 3:30pm PST — calendar invite sent to Alex + Maya. We'll run a 30–40 minute agenda:

1) Quick product intro (5m)
2) Architecture deep-dive: GitHub App model, token rotation, and webinar delivery semantics (15m)
3) Deployment options: hosted vs private gateway (10m)
4) Q&A and next steps (10m)

Notes on the 403: the most common causes are missing repo permissions at install time or branch protection that prevents hooks from being registered. From the screenshot it looks like the install flow didn't include the "Admin:repo_hook" scope, which explains the 403 when our service tried to create the webhook. If they reinstall the App and ensure org admin consent to repo hooks it should succeed. We'll ask for the full log during the call.

Attached: redwood-integration-guide.pdf, architecture-snapshot.png — both include the token rotation flow and retry/backoff behavior for webhooks. Priyom — we'll need you on the call for the private-deploy flow and network considerations.

See you Wed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
